### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-chatbot.mdx`  _(via parseAskQuestionEnvelope (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b5809b323afc1467175a5fecc460aae16f1b49ee` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d48dd333cd4e412e121011205814e624dc38d798` — the merge of head `3a20ecde478fe0712ecbdc1c141d2b1492c20a74` into base `b5809b323afc1467175a5fecc460aae16f1b49ee`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d48dd333cd4e412e121011205814e624dc38d798 && git checkout d48dd333cd4e412e121011205814e624dc38d798
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b5809b323afc1467175a5fecc460aae16f1b49ee 3a20ecde478fe0712ecbdc1c141d2b1492c20a74 && git checkout -B drift-repro b5809b323afc1467175a5fecc460aae16f1b49ee && git merge --no-ff 3a20ecde478fe0712ecbdc1c141d2b1492c20a74

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b5809b323afc1467175a5fecc460aae16f1b49ee
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b5809b323afc1467175a5fecc460aae16f1b49ee` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### Contract review brief — PR #38004 @ `19d67fd4b372d42b3761b88dab5d455f1c5b3b2a` (card #37874)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths packages/spec/src/ai/ask-question.zod.ts` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #37874: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #38004: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `19d67fd4b372d42b3761b88dab5d455f1c5b3b2a`
  · the check-runs on `19d67fd4b372d42b3761b88dab5d455f1c5b3b2a`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: packages/spec/src/ai/ask-question.zod.ts;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `SCRATCHPAD/pr-38004/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `19d67fd4b372d42b3761b88dab5d455f1c5b3b2a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/ask-question.zod.ts + ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/chat/pendingQuestion.ts, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/chat/questionSkip.ts, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/chat/composerGate.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/chat/questionMessage.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/ChatbotEnhanced.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/QuestionCard.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/chat/types.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useChatConversation.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/ChatPane.tsx

Read, not reviewed: `packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts`, `ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/toolResultParsers.ts` (`parseResultEnvelope`), `ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/hitlContinuation.ts`, `ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/AiChatPage.tsx` and the message mappers in `useChatConversation.ts`, all at this head; card #37874 with its five comments (carrier note 7219023636, claim 7220470053, amendments 7220504306 and 7221881624, the os-dev-report 7221811294); topic #37871; the E1 answer 7219010387; the Q1 record 7218887245 and the Q2a L1 note 7218647154. Not readable from this seat: `objectstack-ai/cloud` (the `ask_which` producer and the E1 measurement files), so the E1 figures are taken from the answer as written.

Check-runs on this head when read: 66 in total, 22 success, 9 skipped, 0 failed, 35 still in progress. Success so far: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates, Lint · ESLint, Build Docs, Check Documentation Links. Not concluded: Test Core (10 shards), Test UI (16 shards), Build Core, Type Check · workspace, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI and four Lint and Type Check families. This record judges the diff by reading; it answers for no gate that has not concluded, and those conclusions are still owed before the PR is queued. The PR is a draft.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Legacy accept set: a widening, and only a widening.** On `main` a `status: 'asked_which'` value is read through the loose legacy object, converted, and parsed by `AskQuestionEnvelopeSchema`. At this head it is read through the same loose object, then through an unexported `AskWhichLegacyQuestionSchema`. Rule by rule the two agree except one: `success: true`; `reply` a non-empty string (was `min(1)` on the envelope, now `reply.length === 0` refuses); `question` 1 to 120 and not blank; 2 to 4 readings; each reading non-empty and not blank; no duplicate after trimming (the same `refineOptions`, now shared); unknown top-level keys ignored. The one difference is the reading length: 1 to 24 before, 1 to 60 now. **Accepted now and refused before: exactly the legacy results in which at least one reading is 25 to 60 UTF-16 code units long and every other rule already held.** Nothing accepted before is refused now. The "empty reply is refused" line in the PR body is not a new refusal: the envelope refused it on `main`. Right.
- **Output of the reader widens with it.** `parseAskQuestionEnvelope` can now answer an envelope whose option labels run to 60, typed as `AskQuestionEnvelopeParsed`. The value has the same keys as before (`success`, `status: 'asked'`, `reply`, one question with `question` and `options` of `label` only). A reader that relied on labels of at most 24 would see longer ones; the only reader in the tree is the card in this diff, which wraps them. Declared in the changeset. Right.
- **The `asked` arm does not move.** `AskQuestionOptionSchema`, `AskQuestionSchema` and `AskQuestionEnvelopeSchema` keep their shapes and limits; the `superRefine` callback only gained a name. A label of 25 is still refused there, with a test. Right.
- **`ASK_QUESTION_LIMITS` gains `legacyReadingMaxLength: 60`.** One added key on an exported constant; nothing removed or re-valued. Right.
- **Public surface of `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot`, added only.** `ChatbotEnhancedProps.conversationId` (optional) and the export `QUESTION_SKIP_STORAGE_PREFIX` on the barrel and on `/core`. `QuestionCardOption` and `QuestionCardQuestion` keep their names and fields and become aliases of the spec's parsed types, with `options` still read-only, as the Q2a L1 note asked. They change from interfaces to type aliases, which matters only to a consumer that merges declarations into them; none exists in the tree. Right.
- **The 60 is the E1 figure.** The answer measured 53 readings, 37 over 24, median 29, longest 54, none over 60, and proposed 60 as "the new envelope's `description` cap". The code sets 60, the same number as `descriptionMaxLength`, as its own literal, and keeps 24 and 60 for the new envelope. Right.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are present and identical in the PR body and in both changesets. `none` is the right kind: the diff changes what a tool-result reader accepts and adds console props and exports; no published schema changes shape, and no metadata key, value or type is added or removed. By AGENTS.md, `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`:

- `.changeset/37874-ask-which-reading-length.md`: `@objectstack/spec` patch. Right. Its widening sentence names exactly the delta derived in ①.
- `.changeset/37874-question-card-wiring.md`: `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot` patch and `@object-ui/app-shell` patch. Right. Its widening sentence names exactly the three surface changes in ①.

The three packages the diff moves are the three the changesets name. No narrowing, so no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. `Check Changeset` is success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the dev report. Nothing to answer.
- **Dev flag, `out_of_scope_findings`: the plugin-chatbot README paragraph is outside the claimed surface.** Answered by claim amendment 2 (7221881624), which adds the README, the generated `ask-question.mdx` and the strictness-ledger counts to the surface.
- **Dev flag, PR acceptance notes: `ChatPane.tsx` is also in #37970.** Answered by amendment 1 (7220504306): a serial constraint, the second to land merges main first. The change here is one prop.
- **Dev flag: `Refs #37874`, not `Fixes`.** Right: the card's item 9 (the brightrule smoke after release) is not in this PR and is the maintainer's.
- **Dev flag: no new i18n keys.** Holds: the one string the new message uses, `chatbot.questionCard.aiAsks`, is in all 11 locale packs on `main`.
- **E1, escalated by the Q1 record.** Answered by 7219010387 and carried here by the seat route in 7219023636; the diff implements that route and nothing beyond it.
- SQL push-down: the diff holds no query, no id materialisation and no join. Not applicable.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/ai/ask-question.zod.ts`** against the E1 answer, topic decisions D1 and D2, and its first reader in this diff.

- The legacy arm does what the E1 route says and no more (①). Tried to break the "widening only" claim: an empty reply, a whitespace-only reading, a reading equal to another after trimming, one reading, five readings, a question of 121, a reading of 61, `success: false`, extra keys. Each answers as it did on `main`.
- The `reply` describe, "The console draws the card only when this equals the last assistant text", now has its reader. `questionInSegment` in `pendingQuestion.ts` returns a question only when the segment's last shown assistant text, at or after the message that carries the tool result, equals `reply`; the card, the in-thread message and the hidden Regenerate all read that one answer. The sentence is true at this head, with the nuance in N1.
- Q1's N1 closes. (a) The reader exists, as above. (b) The module JSDoc's "peels the wrapper itself (`parseResultEnvelope`), then hands the object to `parseAskQuestionEnvelope`" is `questionOf` line for line, and a `null` answer leaves the message drawn as its text. (c) The card now reads `ASK_QUESTION_LIMITS.maxOptions` for its digit keys. "Nothing here is stored as turn state and no endpoint takes an answer" still holds: the answer goes out through `onSendMessage`.
- The legacy section of the JSDoc agrees with the code: its own limit for a reading, every other limit the envelope's, and the three refusals it lists.
- N1 (nit) — "equals" is compared after trimming both sides (`content.trim()` against `reply.trim()`), and a test fixes that on purpose. The describe says "equals". A producer reading the describe loses nothing by it; one clause in the describe would make it exact.
- N2 (nit) — two sentences are looser than the code. The `legacyReadingMaxLength` comment says "Readings were never held to the label limit"; the producer never held them, but this reader did on `main`. And a value the legacy arm answers is typed `AskQuestionEnvelopeParsed` although it would not re-validate against `AskQuestionEnvelopeSchema` when a label is over 24; the function's JSDoc says so, the type cannot. Left as written.

**`ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/chat/pendingQuestion.ts`** against the card's item 1 and the envelope contract.

- One parser. The file imports `parseAskQuestionEnvelope` and nothing in `ui/packages` outside tests spells `asked_which`, `asked` as a status, or a limit of its own. The legacy arm, the limits and every refusal are therefore the spec's, and a malformed or over-limit result reaches the console as `null` and draws as text.
- The eight conditions of item 1, each found in the code: stream ended (`status`, and no message still `streaming`); an envelope after the last user message, in both shapes (the segment rule); `reply` equals the last assistant text; no user message after it (the last segment must end the list, and a HITL continuation is a user message); nothing queued; no undecided approval in the segment; not skipped; not `readOnly`.
- Tried to break the gate. A question that is not the last turn: the segment no longer ends the list, no card, and `findQuestions` still draws it as past. A reply that is not the last assistant text, or a later text message in the same segment: no card and no question message. Two questions in one batch: the count is 2, no card. A failed tool, an input-only state, a result that is not an object or carries no `status`: no card. A skipped question after a remount with the same conversation id: stays skipped, with a test. The pane is keyed on the conversation id and remounts when the first send mints it, so no question can be skipped under an undefined id in the console. Tool-call ids on a reload are the stored call ids the result rows are merged by, so the skip key matches across the two shapes. Every case I could not make hold errs towards the plain text and the composer, which is topic acceptance 6.
- The reader keys on the result's `status`, not on the tool's name. That is the contract as written (D2: the envelope is the one shape), noted so that it is a known property.

**`ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/chat/questionSkip.ts`**, **`useChatConversation.ts`**, **`ChatPane.tsx`**, **`chat/types.ts`** against item 7.

- What is stored: one localStorage key per conversation, `objectstack:ai-chat-question-skip:` plus the conversation id, whose value is a JSON list of tool-call ids. Nothing else: no question text, no option, no answer. This is item 7 word for word, and the prop's JSDoc, the constant's JSDoc and the changeset each say the same. Reads and writes are in try/catch; a value that is not a list reads as empty. The prefix shares no prefix with the two chat-cache prefixes, so no existing loop mistakes it for a message cache, and `purgeChatCaches` now clears it on sign-out, with a test.
- The summary stores nothing. It is derived from the message list on each render; the answered-question state that brings the card back after a refused send is component state.
- N3 (nit) — the skip key outlives its conversation's message cache: only sign-out removes it. It holds ids only. Follow-up material if conversation deletion ever clears local state.

**`composerGate.tsx`**, **`ChatbotEnhanced.tsx`**, **`questionMessage.tsx`**, **`QuestionCard.tsx`** against items 3 to 6.

- The composer is rendered as the gate's child in every state, `hidden` and `inert` while the card holds the place, so it is never unmounted (item 3). The card is answered through `onSendMessage` (item 4), stays mounted but hidden after an answer, and returns with its choice if the answer is rolled back. The message layer draws the question from the envelope, pending without options and past with them, and Copy still copies `message.content` (item 5). Regenerate is hidden exactly while the question is pending (item 6). On a `readOnly` transcript there is no card and the question draws as past (topic acceptance 5).
- N4 (nit) — a message that draws as a question no longer draws its answer blocks, so a chart carried by the same streamed message would not show while the turn reads as a question. A turn that ends on a clarifying question normally has none. Left as is.

## 席位核对 — L1 @ `19d67fd4b372d42b3761b88dab5d455f1c5b3b2a`

**Verdict: ACCEPT.** The contract review on this head is PASS: comment 7222001372 (brief 7221915957), `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, no must-fix and no should-fix. The diff is not Tier H: no governed path, no narrowing, 1219 changed lines. The seat lands it once C4 #37970 has landed and this branch has merged `main`. They share `ChatPane.tsx`, and a merge-only delta follows that merge.

### Checklist

- **Shape and relation.** Draft against base `main`. The first line is `Refs #37874 (items 1-8)`, and no closing keyword binds any card. `Refs` is right because item 9, the brightrule smoke after release, belongs to the maintainer, so #37874 stays open and keeps `pm:dispatched`.
  - Q2a #37932 has merged, which was blocked-by.
  - #37799 has merged.
  - C5 #37861 is a soft order, still open; whichever lands later rebases.
- **Items 1–8 against the diff.**
  1. `findPendingQuestion` holds every condition in the card's list 1.1–1.8. It keeps one segment rule for both the streamed and reloaded shapes. The fixtures cover the streamed shape, the reloaded shape, queued, HITL, and two questions in one batch (`pendingQuestion-37874`, 17 cases).
  2. There are two states, pending and past.
  3. `ComposerGate` keeps `PromptInput` mounted, `hidden` and `inert`, and gives focus back when it closes.

- **Scope.** 23 files, all inside the claim (7220470053) and its amendments 7220504306 (`ChatPane.tsx`) and 7221881624 (the README paragraph, `ask-question.mdx` and the ledger counts, both generated). No locale pack is touched.
- **Changesets, read sentence by sentence.**
  - `37874-ask-which-reading-length.md` (`@objectstack/spec` patch). Each of the following is true at this head:
    - the widening, stated exactly: a legacy reading of up to 60 characters is accepted, and nothing newly refused;
    - `legacyReadingMaxLength: 60`;
    - the E1 figures (7219010387: 37 of 53 over 24, max 54);
    - "every other rule still applies". An empty reply was already refused on `main` through the envelope's `reply.min(1)`.
  - `37874-question-card-wiring.md` (`@object-ui/plugin-chatbot`, `@object-ui/app-shell` patch). Every bullet is true against `pendingQuestion.ts`, `composerGate.tsx`, `questionSkip.ts`, `ChatbotEnhanced.tsx` and `ChatPane.tsx`. Specifically:
    - `QuestionCardQuestion` and `QuestionCardOption` keep their names and shape as aliases of the spec types, with `options` read-only;
    - the new exports are `conversationId` and `QUESTION_SKIP_STORAGE_PREFIX` (index and `/core`).
  - Both levels follow AGENTS.md: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`.
- **Docs.** The `plugin-chatbot.mdx` paragraph and the README paragraph say the same thing, as the page and the package README already do for the card. Every sentence is true at this head. The regenerated `ask-question.mdx` matches the JSDoc.
- **Test and gate evidence.** The os-dev-report (7221811294) is pinned to `19d67fd4`:
  - spec 19/19 and UI 1006/1006 (111 files);
  - `dispatch-gates` 113/113, with 0 NOT-MEASURED;
  - three ablations: the queued condition (2 red), `inert` (1 red), and the legacy limit (1 red);
  - `overlap-check --pr=37970` clean.

  Check-runs at this head: 61 success, 9 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending; `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` green. No dogfood battery is owed: no `!` in the title and no narrowing arm.

### Accepted deviations

- **L2 nits N1–N4 (7222001372)** are accepted with no head move:
  - **N1:** "equals" versus a trimmed compare.
  - **N2:** two loose sentences in `ask-question.zod.ts`.
  - **N3:** the skip key outlives its conversation and is cleared at sign-out.
  - **N4:** a message drawn as a question drops its answer blocks.

  N1 and N2 are prose in a published file. A later spec PR that touches the module can tighten them.
- The report lists the README paragraph as out of scope. Amendment 7221881624 since covers it.
